text:
Burleson & Company LLC raised its holdings in Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 9.0% during the 2nd quarter, Holdings Channel reports. The fund owned 15,475 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after buying an additional 1,276 Apple makes up approximately 1.7% of Burleson & Company LLC’s holdings, making the stock its 12th biggest holding. Burleson & Company LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $2,865,000 at the end of the most recent quarter.
Other institutional investors have also made changes to their positions in the company. Financial Gravity Wealth Inc. bought a new position in shares of Apple during the 1st quarter worth about $491,000. Retirement Planning Group increased its holdings in shares of Apple by 15.0% during the 1st quarter. Retirement Planning Group now owns 9,341 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $1,567,000 after purchasing an additional 1,219 Comerica Securities Inc. increased its holdings in shares of Apple by 4.2% during the 1st quarter. Comerica Securities Inc. now owns 35,603 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,973,000 after purchasing an additional 1,425 Stanley Capital Management LLC increased its holdings in shares of Apple by 6.4% during the 1st quarter. Stanley Capital Management LLC now owns 56,206 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $9,430,000 after purchasing an additional 3,400 Finally, Columbia Asset Management increased its holdings in shares of Apple by 0.6% during the 1st quarter. Columbia Asset Management now owns 92,943 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $15,594,000 after purchasing an additional 523 57.65% of the stock is currently owned by institutional investors.

Over the last 90 days, insiders sold 470,005 shares of company stock worth $104,764,873. Company insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock.
Several research analysts have recently issued reports on the stock. BTIG Research upgraded shares of Apple to a “buy” rating and boosted their price objective for the stock from $207.00 to $235.00 in a report on Wednesday, August 1st. Macquarie set a $214.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a report on Wednesday, August 15th. Morgan Stanley restated a “buy” rating and set a $232.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a report on Wednesday, August 22nd. S&P Equity Research boosted their price objective on shares of Apple to $250.00 and gave the stock an “in-line” rating in a report on Tuesday, September 11th. They noted that the move was a valuation call. Finally, UBS Group assumed coverage on shares of Apple in a report on Wednesday, September 12th. Three analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twenty-three have issued a hold rating and twenty-five have issued a buy rating to the stock. The company currently has an average rating of “Hold” and a consensus target price of $223.07.
NASDAQ:AAPL opened at $172.29 on Friday. The stock has a market capitalization of $868.90 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 14.47, a PEG ratio of 1.27 and a beta of 1.26. Apple Inc. has a 12 month low of $150.24 and a 12 month high of $233.47. The company has a current ratio of 1.12, a quick ratio of 1.09 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, November 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.91 EPS for the quarter, beating the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $2.78 by $0.13. The firm had revenue of $62.90 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $61.55 billion. Apple had a net margin of 22.41% and a return on equity of 48.68%. The company’s revenue for the quarter was up 19.6% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same period in the previous year, the business earned $2.07 earnings per share. Research analysts predict that Apple Inc. will post 13.35 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
The company also recently declared a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, November 15th. Shareholders of record on Monday, November 12th were given a $0.73 dividend. The ex-dividend date was Thursday, November 8th. This represents a $2.92 dividend on an annualized basis and a yield of 1.69%. Apple’s dividend payout ratio (DPR) is presently 24.52%.
